description: The Wood Goat in Chinese astrology: personality, Wood element traits, 1955 and 2015 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Wood Goat is the Goat born in a Wood year, one of five versions of the eighth animal. It combines the Goat's gentleness with Wood's qualities. Wood Goat years between 1924 and 2044 are 1955 and 2015. The Goat's fixed element is Earth.

sections.heading: The Wood Goat personality
paragraphs: For the Wood Goat, Wood controls Earth, and the Goat's fixed element is Earth, so the year stem stirs the animal's settled core, encouraging growth and outward connection. Wood Goats are often described as kind, generous and community-minded, with the sign's artistic sensitivity joined to a strong sense of fairness. They tend to be compassionate helpers, quick to support friends and causes they believe in. Many have a gift for crafts, gardening or music. The stirring influence keeps them engaged with the world, but it can also make them anxious, as Wood's push towards growth unsettles the Goat's need for security, and they may take on too much out of kindness.

In the five-element scheme, Wood belongs to the east and to the green energy of early spring, and that seasonal image shapes how it colours an animal sign. A Wood stem tends to soften sharp edges and add warmth, curiosity and a cooperative instinct. Traditional texts associate it with benevolence, growth and the wish to build something that lasts beyond the self. People born under a Wood stem are often portrayed as principled, open-handed and hopeful about others. The caution usually attached to Wood is a habit of spreading energy thinly, saying yes to every request and feeling quietly hurt when generosity is not returned in kind.

sections.heading: Wood Goat at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, the Wood element is usually linked with planning, teaching and collaborative building. Wood-year people are often described as good at seeing how a team could grow and at nurturing the people inside it, which suits roles in education, design, community work, healthcare and any field with a long horizon. They tend to prefer cooperation over rivalry. The traditional warning is about scope: a Wood stem can start more ventures than it can finish, so firm priorities and honest deadlines usually serve it well.

Kind, artistic and cooperative, the Wood Goat tends to flourish where empathy is part of the job description. Early-years teaching, craft design, community arts, gardening and charity work are commonly associated with it, since gentle persistence creates value in each. A supportive manager, a harmonious team and a little creative licence keep it content, while competitive bonus cultures usually unsettle it. In close relationships the Wood Goat is affectionate, generous and devoted to making home feel welcoming, often with fresh flowers and something baking. It wants security and appreciation. People-pleasing is the quiet hazard: it may agree to arrangements it secretly dislikes, then feel hurt that its partner never guessed.

sections.heading: Wood Goat years and dates
paragraphs: Wood Goat years in the Lunar New Year table run from January 24, 1955 to February 11, 1956 and from February 19, 2015 to February 7, 2016. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 2015 anyone born before Feb 19 is a Wood Horse, not a Wood Goat. Sixty years separate each Wood Goat year, the length of a full round of five elements and twelve animals. Every Wood Goat year is Yin, matching the Goat's own polarity.

Its traditional name is Yi-Wei: Yi is the yin Wood stem and Wei is the Goat's branch. Births just before each new year fall in the Wood Horse year (before January 24, 1955) and the Wood Horse year (before February 19, 2015), and births in the weeks after each Wood Goat year ends belong to the Fire Monkey. The new year itself fell on a Monday in 1955 and Thursday in 2015.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Wood Goat
paragraphs: Wood Goats tend to benefit from protecting their generosity with gentle boundaries. Deciding in advance how much time and energy to give to a cause helps prevent overextension. Because they can worry about others' approval, building confidence in their own judgement is useful; keeping a record of decisions that turned out well can help. Wood Goats often flourish in collaborative creative settings where kindness is valued. Time spent among plants and in nature restores them. When they let themselves receive as well as give, Wood Goats become the warm centre of any community.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Wood Goat shares the Goat's San He trine with the Rabbit and Pig (the Wood trine), its Liu He bond with the Horse, and its Liu Chong clash with the Ox. The element adds a second layer: another Wood sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Wood in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Wood Goat years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1955 (from January 24, 1955) and 2015 (from February 19, 2015). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Wood Goat's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Wood and the Goat's fixed element is Earth; in the five-element cycles wood controls Earth. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Wood Goat?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Rabbit and Pig (San He) and the Horse (Liu He). The Ox is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Wood Goat called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Yi-Wei. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Wood stem Yi, followed by its earthly branch, here Wei for the Goat, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Wood Goat different from other Goats?
faq.answer: All Goats share gentleness, creativity and empathy. The Wood year element changes the tone: wood is the element of spring and of things that grow, so a Wood year is traditionally said to lend any animal a generous, expansive streak.
